title: Epochal span stabilizer: async context safety and sampling-hints bridge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: async request flows (worker fanout, websockets, retries) frequently break span boundaries in our SDKs and middleware. Root causes include: lost context during task rehydration, non-deterministic re-ordering of callback lifecycles, and legacy propagators that overwrite sampling hints. This leads to broken trace trees, noisy orphan spans, and incorrect sampling decisions for high-QPS endpoints.

Objective: implement an 'epochal span stabilizer' in SDKs and middleware that: (1) pins an ephemeral epoch token to a request envelope to allow safe re-attachment of spans across async boundaries; (2) preserves sampling_hint and sampling_reason through legacy/third-party propagators; (3) exposes opt-in low-overhead hooks to the runtime for opportunistic span stitching and deduplication. The feature must be backward compatible with existing OTEL-compatible collectors and our sidecar trace gateway.

Approach: 1) Add a compact epoch token (6 bytes base64) placed in two carriers: X-RW-Epoch and an envelope-level baggage key. 2) Implement a lightweight stabilizer library in the Node/Python/Go SDKs that: attaches epoch to outgoing child spans, checks for epoch mismatch on incoming requests and attempts deterministic reconciliation (prefer epoch on request owner). 3) Export sampling_hint as a separate header X-RW-Sampling-Hint and add a reconciliation step in the SDK to avoid being overridden by legacy 'sampled' flags. 4) Add middleware adapters for Express/FastAPI/gRPC interceptors and the worker queue adapters (Celery/RQ/Kafka consumers) to restore context from epoch tokens on task startup. 5) Build a debugging mode that logs reconciliation events to a dedicated debug metric: rw.tracing.epoch.reconciliations.

Trade-offs: epoch tokens add minor header overhead and require coordinated rollout across SDKs and edge proxies for maximum fidelity. We will make the feature opt-in by default for non-critical customers and enable-by-default for Redwood-managed services after a staged rollout.

Compatibility notes: When epoch header is absent we fallback to existing propagation semantics. When multiple epochs are present we pick the one with the 'owner' flag or the most recent timestamp embedded in the token. Fallback bridging to legacy propagators keeps legacy 'sampled' header unchanged but preserves our sampling_hint in X-RW-Sampling-Hint to reduce sampling drift.
acceptance_criteria: Epoch token header is present in all outgoing SDK requests when opt-in flag enabled
Middleware adapters restore span context across async worker handoffs in Node/Python/Go integration tests
Sampling_hint header is preserved through proxy-to-service and does not get overwritten by legacy propagators in regression tests
End-to-end trace graphs in staging show >95% successful parent->child linkage for a synthetic fanout workload compared to baseline ~72%
rw.tracing.epoch.reconciliations metric emitted with counts and reconciled_outcome tags
Rollout runbook and rollback path documented and verified in dry-run
testing_plan: Unit tests for token encoding/decoding and collision properties
Integration tests: express->worker->downstream reproducible span linkage using synthetic fanout harness
Chaos test: simulated partial header loss and reordered callbacks to validate reconcilers
Performance benchmark: measure header+stabilizer overhead for p50/p95 latency at 1k RPS in staging
Compatibility tests against OpenTelemetry collector and our trace gateway ensuring no field name collisions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: library-level feature behind feature flag; no default enabled; run long-running staging for 72h
Phase 1: enable in Redwood-managed runtime (internal traffic only) for 1 week; track reconciliation and linkage metrics
Phase 2: opt-in beta for customers via SDK minor release (announce in changelog + migration guide)
Phase 3: gradual enable-by-default for all hosted routes where linkages improved >=20% and no regression signals
Rollback: toggle-off flag and purge rw.tracing.epoch.* debug metrics; revert SDK version in 2-step rollback if consumer-facing regressions observed
notes: Related tickets: ENG-63211 (span-handoff-handshake), ENG-21478 (opaque-metadata-gateway) -- used for integration checks
UX: include debug header echoing in dev console to assist customers with adoption
